environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; openssl s_client for SNI, strict upstream peer

findings.description: sni_cb serves the certificate named by SNI and does nothing else; the callback never touches the route pointer, so a certificate is chosen for a name the request need not come from.
findings.title: Host and SNI are independent authorities and are never reconciled

findings.description: One TLS connection with SNI beta.test and Host alpha.test serves certificate CN=beta.test, passes hostname verification for beta.test, and the request executes on alpha's proxied exec route: the client verifies one name and runs code on another. Precondition: a TLS listener with two server_name blocks each carrying its own proxied location.
findings.title: Host and SNI are independent authorities and are never reconciled

findings.description: The forwarded request always carries the constant Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>; the client Host is consumed for routing and dropped, so an upstream that routes on Host sees the proxy's constant regardless of what the client sent.
findings.title: Host and SNI are independent authorities and are never reconciled

findings.description: server_name arguments are stored with lower() and no grammar check, so a trailing-dot name loads and its certificate is served by SNI, while every Host carrying the same trailing dot is rejected by the Host validator: the name is reachable by cert and unreachable by route.
findings.title: Host and SNI are independent authorities and are never reconciled

limitations: All RCE is on the upstream host
Needs a TLS listener and two server blocks
An exec route must be proxied on the routed vhost to show command output
methods: Read the release source from the tag

Control pair first, then the crossed SNI/Host matrix
Compared the served certificate subject with the executed route
